children: Shantanu Nandan Sharma Tirupati: Call it the AC industry's cool migration - from the North to South India. Enthused by the Centre's production linked incentive (PLI) scheme and the strategic need to be closer to fast-growing southern markets, leading air-conditioner makers are redrawing India's manufacturing map. In the last five years, major AC makers such as Daikin, Blue Star, LG, Carrier and Havells Lloyd have opened new factories in Sri City, Andhra Pradesh. Also, Voltas, a Tata Group company, and Mitsubishi Electric recently established AC manufacturing units in neighbouring Tamil Nadu. These facilities along with Samsung India's existing plant in Sriperumbudur are turning the 100-km Sriperumbudur-Chennai-Sri City corridor into the country's newest - and hottest - AC manufacturing belt.

Ravindra Sannareddy, co-founder and managing director of Sri City, an 8,500-acre private industrial city in Andhra's Tirupati district bordering Tamil Nadu, told ET that the city he built in 2008 has now emerged as a magnet for India's AC industry, among others. Sri City has attracted investments from as many as 10 AC manufacturers-both global and Indian companies-and 34 component suppliers over the past five years.

title: Migration in Full Swing, AC Cos are Making South Cooler
